newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Ag Min would be opposed to new soybean tax.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Ag Min would be opposed to new soybean tax.

text.p: Brazilian soybean crushers have not called on the government to levy a new tax on soybean exports and would be rejected if they ever made such a demand, Brazil's Agriculture Ministry said.
"Officially, I have received no document (requesting a new soybean tax)," said Favio Pereira, adviser at the ministry's Agricultural Policy Secretariat.
"It is politically absurd and unviable. The Agriculture Ministry is opposed to the idea, clearly opposed," he added.

Crushers have complained that they are at a disadvantage to their counterparts in other countries since the government abolished the ICMS tax on exports, which was 13 percent on soybeans, 11.1 percent on soymeal and eight percent on soyoil.
"There was a three percent tax advantage for soy products," said Pereira. "When the government decided to stimulate exports by abolishing the ICMS tax on all products, the benefit stopped."
Crushers are demanding the Brazilian government hold talks with its Mercosur trade partner Argentina, which they say maintains a tax structure that favours local crushers.
"There are two very large crushers in particular which they are worried about," Pereira said.

In addition, crushers were asking to be covered by a tax rebate law under which they could be reimbursed for the tax soybean producers have already paid on production components such as fertilizers and machinery.
The government has yet to respond to either demand.
